record_notes.DCP-LETT-1382: Incoming fragment conjectured circa April 1851 from the Pickering enclosure and Hooker return from India, not an exact April day. Thanks for a just-received Darwin letter and enclosure, proposes complete island floras across subsidence stages, and distinguishes small islands with peculiar plants from coral islets. The Martin comparison ends in an explicit missing-page marker. Final barnacle/fern sentence was physically at the top, not a second dated letter. Darwin pencil comments and portfolio number are separate undated layers. The forwarding Darwin cover is unlocated; prior 1300 and 1339 do not contain this forwarding event. Pickering is not Hooker or Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1440: Incoming fragment begins mid-sentence, then temporary Kew housing, paid editorship of 36 exhibition jury reports, wife returned from a trip, salmon/lake-trout hybrid inquiry and winter freshwater herring report. Late August–early September 1851 comes from housing history; broad XML August–September bounds do not supply a day. Footnote 8 contains separate unidentified-correspondent scraps, Darwin notes, and published historical claims about fish; not all are this Hooker letter or contemporary knowledge gained on its composition date. Later Origin/Variation citations and undated portfolio marks do not prove receipt or reading by a precise day. No uniquely matched Darwin response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1460: November 1851 incoming fragment starts mid-thought. Lyall collection, Oxalis synonymy and eight names for one variable species, Alseuosmia and uncertain Coprosma delimitation lead Hooker to reject a simple insular-variability rule while becoming more persuaded of a former southern continent. His own caveat about being influenced by Cunningham errors must remain. European grasses absent in Australia and Owen review complaint conclude the source. Later flora counts and diagnoses are editorial comparisons, not replacements for this letter. Darwin November pencil label supports dating but supplies no exact receipt date. Later manuscript discussions in 1532/1529 are not automatically replies to this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1496: April 1852 queries memorandum with a separate draft used to identify recipient and date, not an ordinary dated incoming-prompt/outgoing-answer exchange. Eight extracted paragraphs preserve the original numbering, including repeated 6: geographical variability, local versus widespread species, organ variation, unusual development, variable genera, and self-fertilisation. Hooker pencilled answers ARE preserved in footnotes, including stamens, Nepenthes, variable genera and aquatic plants. Darwin later overwrote or extended answers and added references to 1853 Lindley/Flora and 1855 Miers. Those added layers cannot inherit April 1852. Do not promote embedded Hooker answers into a fabricated letter or treat later Darwin additions as an 1852 reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1532: September 25 with supplied 1853 year reviews the introductory-essay manuscript for Flora Novae-Zelandiae. Darwin discusses neutral naming consequences of species mutability and repeated taxonomic revisions, praises the journal illustrations, suggests a more precise Himalayan title, requests a German distribution notice, and reports finishing Esmond while other books barely begun. This is a manuscript review plus unlocated covering correspondence, not a reply to Hooker 1319 from 1850. Source distinguishes currently reviewed introductory paper, prospective remainder and future Darwin species volume. Published bibliographic forms do not replace the manuscript version.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1529: October 9, 1853 is an editorial reconstruction from the next-day 8 AM coach dispatch, not a dateline in this manuscript. Detailed comments cover pages 30–43 and 71–72, including Bory, fern hybrids, phrasing, Edwardsia/Oxalis currents, island genus size, Eucalyptus, European plants and tributes. The raw diag/ramme strings are source presentation artifacts, not scientific words to silently edit in the frozen projection. Hooker considerate note arrived during Darwin reading, but its text is unlocated. A Kew visit is intended for next summer, not completed. Forbes professorship remains prospective; later 1854 appointment belongs only to apparatus. Shared taxa with 1460 do not establish that old letter as the prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1535: October 10, 1853 Monday reports this morning 8 AM coach dispatch of manuscript, borrowed books and the accompanying letter identified editorially as 1529. Instructions to book onward by delivery company and hope that parcel arrives before this note are prospective, not confirmed receipt. Ruth has just been begun, not completed. One dispatch witness and no preserved incoming request; does not form an incoming/outgoing pair with his own preceding letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1539: Friday morning assigned November 4, 1853, after November 3 council vote and before Darwin November 5 answer. Hooker reports nomination, recess inquiries, final vote, support for Lindley rather than Darwin, and wife slow recovery. Independently inspected MathML: raw 23 and 34 are two-thirds and three-quarters, not integer vote totals. Distinguish June nomination, November vote, and later November 30 presentation; the latter and Tyndall episode are editorial context. Family visit remains an intention. Directly answered by 1540.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1540: November 5, 1853 gives explicit same-morning receipt and opening order: missing Sabine notice first, Hooker 1539 second. The same medal news produced a different emotional response through friendship. Lindley nomination, Mrs Hooker slow recovery, widened medal eligibility and foreign evidence specifically match 1539; gratitude is a direct answer. Sabine original is missing and must not be reconstructed. Finishing second volume is prospective; 1854 proofs are later apparatus. All body paragraphs read, with P4 valediction and P5–7 post-closing continuation retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1552F: Thursday afternoon is one of two mutually exclusive dates, February 9 or 16, 1854, not a continuous date interval or an automatically chosen February 16. Book arrived within minutes. Darwin has seen dedication and some illustrations but has not read the title page or all illustrations; Emma then has the book. Reading this evening and setting aside Stansbury are intentions. Later March 7 and March 23 reading-notebook entries must not be imported as completed February reading. Mrs Hooker assistance is credited, not equal authorship of every page. No preserved covering incoming letter; reverse acknowledgement in 1557 answers his gratitude.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1557: Sunday assigned February 26, 1854. P1 explicitly answers Darwin kind hearty acceptance of the dedication in 1552F and explains its Antarctic-voyage origin. P2 reflects on ambition and family, followed by wife health after a walk, response to Lyell lava-slope news, expected Henslow visit, Tasmania grant and six-copy obligation, and sold-out travels with profits still unknown. Only P1 is a demonstrated reply to 1552F. Lyell source letter identity remains ambiguous between January Madeira and a possible February Tenerife letter; no invented Darwin reading or exact cross-correspondent edge. Future delivery of Flora Tasmanica and unborn child are not accomplished facts. Undated Darwin marks separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1300: Prior explicit primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and raw source hashes. February3 with editorial1850 year: newspaper first brought imprisonment news, then Darwin wrote Henslow and received a note from Sir William through that route. This is distinct from any direct incoming J.D.Hooker prompt. Liberation is hoped to occur before letter arrival, not known; continuing collecting and return home are conditional. Health plateau, cold baths, no Royal Society council attendance yet; later February7 attendance belongs only to editorial future. Fossil barnacles frustrate him, fourth son/seventh child born, chloroform administered before doctor arrived are historical reports. Requests Falconer news and sends regards; old1220 provides continuing background but does not establish immediate reply identity. Final Fitton shipwreck report follows January24 newspaper about June1849 event: distinguish news publication from event date and do not reconstruct newspaper wording as an incoming letter. Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1319: Prior explicit primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and raw source hashes. Two composition sections, April6 Government House and April7 Botanic Gardens, not mutually exclusive alternative dates. April6P1–6 responds to earlier full letters received about two months previously:1260 is identified by species-versus-barnacle preference and correction of Yangma dam to moraine. Hooker says theories interest but do not convert him, reports well-marked Sikkim willows/Rubi/Senecios/Gnaphalia despite equable climate and revises Himalayan drainage, snowline and glacier model. Falconer/Thomson and Humboldt views are attributed, current theory provisional. April7P8 recounts five-month parcel withholding, seven Frances letters released, reconciliation and good health; only later within this section explicitly acknowledges February letter received this morning and responds to incomplete cure and seven children, identifying1300. Do not let this April7 input condition April6 prose. Nepal permission attempt fails, Sylhet/Khassya/Manipur journey and Thomson joining prospective; later May1 departure is editorial. Footnote2 preserves an original Darwin abstract of this letter plus later marks: its April6 label dates the source letter, not Darwin taking notes that day in England.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1339: Prior explicit primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and raw source hashes. June13 with supplied1850 year, written Malvern while source letters locked atDown. Last letter received about fortnight ago gives approximate late-May event, not exactMay30. This answer combines1257 and1319: P2 poem, cold-finger SouthAmerica reading, inverted strata and P6 Malcolmson correction match1257; glacier continuity and transverse rivers also engage1319. P3 philosophical-mind reassurance answers1319P4 self-deprecation. Most decisively P5 explicitly answers1319P2 theory-effect question and P3 distinct Sikkim Rubi/willows versus NorthAmerica, not merely independent Darwin news. P6 forgives/reconciled Falconer response is additional exact match. Water cure progress remains mixed; fossil pedunculate book going to press is an intention, not1851 publication accomplished. Source-year/preprint bibliography must not overwrite contemporary availability. One joint answer, not duplicate independent whole-letter examples.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1371: Prior explicit primary reading reused with matching note, ledger and raw source hashes. November26Silchar: acknowledges letter debt and explains renewed Falconer withholding; routine for three months afterApril followed by six mails missing, while an English proof parcel actually arrived today without letter and was discarded. Retain exception to rhetorical sends nothing. Current/anticipated route via Manipurfrontier, Sylhet, Chittagong, Arracan/Ceylon and return is prospective. P7–14 specifically answers1339 transverse-river/double-chain argument, distinguishes watershed axis from line of highest snowy peaks using labeled diagram, tests definitions of geological/geographical chain and argues denudation/river organization; does not simply accept two parallel chains. P15 report of Darwin BritishAssociation presence concerns1849meeting via delayed news, not proof1850attendance. P16 records roots in underclay but failed search for McClelland fossil beach, distant views stated as estimates. P17 promises barnacles, contrasts tropical low-altitude oaks and high palms with fossil-climate assumptions, adds Tibetan camel/elephant reports; later journal says barnacles notcollected, so promise is not shipment. P18 classifies Khasi boulders as denudation rather than ice. Expects reunion before an answer, not proof no answer exists. One source diagram and separate undated Darwin pencil score read.
